# ui::testing::WindowSeams

Header: `winui/testing/WindowSeams.hpp`.

Installs platform services on a [Window](../tree/window.md): its host, compositor, native host, spell checker and context-menu host. The clipboard and the launcher belong to the whole process instead, so a test swaps them with [set_clipboard()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_clipboard) and [set_launcher()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_launcher).

A window gets these from whatever hosts it. The backend installs the real ones when it creates the native window, and [HeadlessUI](headless-ui.md) installs its own. A test uses this to hand the window a test double. Every pointer is non-owning and must outlive the window's use of it; nullptr removes the service. Get one with [seams()](namespace-ui-testing.md#seams).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Window                       window;
ui::testing::TestContextMenuHost menu;
ui::testing::seams(window).set_context_menu_host(&menu);
```

## effective_style

```cpp
WindowStyle effective_style() const
```

style() with `Frame::Themed` resolved against the current theme, the style the native window runs with. That is `Borderless` while the theme draws the frame and `Standard` when it has none. Every other frame passes through.

## drawn_frame_border

```cpp
float drawn_frame_border() const
```

The width in DIPs of the border the theme draws, which is also the resize band; 0 when the OS draws the frame.

## caption_icon

```cpp
const Bitmap& caption_icon() const
```

The icon a caption the theme draws shows when the window's icon() has no image or glyph of its own, as the host reported it; empty until it reports one.

## drawn_title_bar

```cpp
Element* drawn_title_bar() const
```

The caption the theme draws, as an automation node (a [TitleBar](../controls/title-bar.md#uititlebar) holding the caption buttons) for the host to list before the content; nullptr when the OS draws the frame.

## wants_blur_behind

```cpp
bool wants_blur_behind() const
```

Whether the frame the theme draws is glass and wants the desktop behind the window blurred: Aero's frame, while transparency effects are on and the window is not full screen. The host answers with [report_blur_behind()](#report_blur_behind).

## frame_corner_cut

```cpp
std::span<const std::uint8_t> frame_corner_cut() const
```

The rounded top corners of the frame the theme draws, as the pixels to cut off each top corner, one entry per row from the top, at 96 DPI. Empty for a square frame, while the window is maximized or full screen, and while the frame is glass. The host shapes the window with it.

## blur_behind

```cpp
bool blur_behind() const
```

Whether the host reported the blur as live ([report_blur_behind()](#report_blur_behind)).

## handle_external_drag_enter

```cpp
DragResponse handle_external_drag_enter(DataPackage data, Point position)
```

A drag from another app has come over the window at `position`, in client DIPs, carrying `data`. The drop targets there are asked as for a drag inside the app; returns their answer. Refused while a drag inside the app is running.

## handle_external_drag_over

```cpp
DragResponse handle_external_drag_over(Point position, std::optional<DataPackageOperation> requested = std::nullopt)
```

The drag from another app moved to `position`; `requested` replaces the operation the package asks for (the keys held changed it). Returns the answer there.

## handle_external_drag_leave

```cpp
void handle_external_drag_leave()
```

The drag from another app left the window, or was canceled.

## handle_external_drag_drop

```cpp
DataPackageOperation handle_external_drag_drop(Point position)
```

The drag from another app was released at `position`. Returns what the drop did, None when nothing took it.

## handle_external_drop

```cpp
DataPackageOperation handle_external_drop(DataPackage data, Point position)
```

Files dropped on the window from another app at `position`, reported only on release: the enter and the drop at once. Returns what the drop did, None when nothing took it.
